research_question: Why do people commonly recommend eight hours of sleep, and what does sleep science actually establish about duration, biological function, and individual variation?
method: Authoritative-source synthesis. The connected Elicit API returned an account-plan access denial, so no Elicit report is claimed.

sources.title: Recommended Amount of Sleep for a Healthy Adult: A Joint Consensus Statement of the American Academy of Sleep Medicine and Sleep Research Society
sources.publisher: Journal of Clinical Sleep Medicine / AASM and Sleep Research Society
notes: The consensus recommends adults sleep at least seven hours regularly for optimal health.
Regular sleep below seven hours is associated with multiple adverse health and performance outcomes.
The statement notes that more than nine hours may be appropriate for some groups, including young adults and people recovering from sleep debt or illness.

sources.title: About Sleep
sources.publisher: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
notes: Sleep needs vary by age and person; adult recommendations are not identical to recommendations for children and teenagers.
Sleep supports health, emotional well-being, attention, and memory.
Sleep quality and regularity matter alongside duration.

sources.title: Sleep Deprivation and Deficiency
sources.publisher: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute, NIH
notes: Sleep deficiency can involve too little sleep, poor-quality sleep, sleeping at the wrong time, or a sleep disorder.
Sleep deficiency can affect learning, focus, reaction time, decision-making, and emotional regulation.
Chronic insufficient sleep is linked with a range of health problems.

sources.title: Brain Basics: Understanding Sleep
sources.publisher: National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke, NIH
notes: Sleep is an active biological process, not simply inactivity.
Sleep cycles through non-REM and REM stages; patterns change across the night.
Researchers continue to investigate the full set of functions sleep serves.

sources.title: How Much Sleep Do We Really Need?
sources.reliability: Sleep-health educational publisher summarizing expert recommendations
notes: Eight hours is a useful public shorthand, not a universal biological quota for every adult.
Recommended duration ranges reflect population evidence and individual variation.
Sleep duration should be interpreted together with daytime alertness and sleep quality.
